summary.title: Threat Model for Spice.ai Enterprise v2.0.0
summary.description: Spice Enterprise is a portable runtime for fast, last-mile SQL query, search, and AI inference.

diagrams.title: Data + AI Runtime (Local/Network)

data.name: Spice Runtime
data.description: Rust daemon exposing SQL, Flight, OpenAI-compatible, MCP, and Iceberg APIs with embedded accelerators. Enterprise v2.0 adds external authentication via API key and OIDC/JWT bearer tokens (with OpenID discovery, JWKS retrieval and refresh, claim mapping, and per-protocol auth middleware) and identity-aware SQL functions (`current_user_id()`, `current_org_id()`, `current_role()`, `session_property()`). v2.0 also adds DDL support (CREATE/DROP TABLE) for Iceberg and Cayenne catalogs, expanded DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) across Cayenne, Snowflake, Postgres, DynamoDB, and Sharepoint plus DuckLake INSERT on read_write catalogs, async query materialization to object storage, distributed ingestion, URL Tables (opt-in SSRF surface), SMB/NFS data connectors, acceleration snapshot management API, public-listener mTLS for HTTP and Flight (`runtime.tls.client_auth_mode` none/request/required), and on-disk TLS cert hot-reload across all TLS endpoints.

threats.title: Task history reset on restart
threats.description: The task history table is only kept in-memory, which means any tasks that would be captured are lost if an attacker wants to conceal what they did by either timing their activity to occur before a maintenance activity that results in a restart, or by purposefully causing the runtime to restart.
threats.mitigation: Persist task_history locally

threats.title: No persistent audit logs
threats.description: Spice does not provide persistent audit logging of actions taken that could repudiate that a certain action was taken. In Enterprise v2.0, callers may be authenticated via API key or OIDC/JWT, so identity context (mapped user_id, org_id, claims) is available for logging — but task history records are not persisted across restarts, so they cannot be relied on as durable audit evidence.
threats.mitigation: Implement a proper audit/task history log tracking both changes to the runtime operation (i.e. modifying Spicepod, runtime settings) as well as data operations (queries, refreshes) that is persistent across restarts.

threats.title: Data source connection details (or any secrets) leaked via errors/logging
threats.description: Metadata about connected data sources is leaked through error messages, revealing sensitive infrastructure details.
threats.mitigation: Review code where logs are emitted to ensure that potential sensitive information (i.e. credentials encoded in headers) is not leaked via error messages. Token redaction in debug/error output has been implemented. The /v1/spicepods endpoint returns summaries instead of full configuration to avoid leaking connection details.

threats.title: Malicious SQL / SQL injection leading to ACE
threats.description: A user exploits a vulnerability in the SQL parser to execute arbitrary code (ACE) on the Spice runtime.
threats.mitigation: Queries that would allow modifying the state of the runtime are rejected at the parsing layer. v2.0 introduces DDL (CREATE TABLE / DROP TABLE) for Iceberg and Cayenne catalogs only; DDL is validated against an allowlist of permitted catalogs and operations. SQL identifier quoting is enforced across all connectors to prevent injection via table/column names. Prepared statements with parameterized queries are used for federated execution.

threats.title: Malicious compressed small payload has unbounded/very large size
threats.description: If an attacker is able to send a payload to a Spice endpoint that is compressed, and the decompression of that payload causes Spice to run out of memory due to the payload itself having a very large/potentially unbounded size - then it could cause a denial of service. (i.e. Zipbomb)
threats.mitigation:
- No known Gzip attack vector and the HTTP endpoints only accept Gzip compression
- For connecting to data sources, we rely on object_store's implementation which should protect against this.

threats.title: Task History shows truncated results
threats.description:
If you have access to the runtime, you can access the task_history table along with some truncated outputs of data you might not normally be able to access.

This isn't a problem in v0.17.4-beta, because if you can access the task_history table, then you trivially can access any of the data sources.
threats.mitigation: No mitigation currently. Once we add AuthN/AuthZ, we will need to design how to lock this down appropriately. (i.e. RLS)

threats.title: Malicious SQL / SQL injection leading to information disclosure
threats.description: If there are functions that allow reading from the environment/file-system, this could lead to unexpected information disclosure of the system details/secrets
threats.mitigation:
- Run in a chroot process with limited file-system access
- Disable functions that allow this access

threats.title: Supply chain attack leading to compromised dependency
threats.description: If an attacker is able to compromise a dependency that we depend on, and we release a version of Spice with that compromised dependency, then all of Spice users would potentially be affected.
threats.mitigation:
- CVE scanner/dependabot to scan for known issues with dependencies
- Adopt a policy of waiting before upgrading a dependency to allow for the community to identify
- Processing scanning to identify suspicious behavior

threats.title: Unprotected control plane endpoints
threats.description: HTTP/Arrow Flight/OpenAI-compatible/MCP/Iceberg APIs accept requests without built-in authentication or rate limits by default. Exposure of these endpoints beyond a trusted network allows attackers to run arbitrary queries or inference, modify runtime state, or exfiltrate data.
threats.mitigation: Terminate traffic behind an API gateway with mTLS/JWT, restrict bind addresses/firewall rules, enable runtime-auth when available, and apply per-endpoint rate limiting before exposing services to untrusted clients.

threats.title: Telemetry and traces leak sensitive data
threats.description: Verbose traces, query logs, or model prompt/response bodies may include secrets or PII that are exported to OTEL/metrics backends without redaction.
threats.mitigation: Default to minimal logging, scrub sensitive fields before emission, isolate telemetry destinations, and apply retention policies/PII filtering in observability pipelines.

threats.title: Unauthorized Iceberg table writes
threats.description: The Iceberg connector supports writes while other data sources are read-only. Without strong authentication, input validation, and authorization, attackers with endpoint access can corrupt, drop, or poison Iceberg tables.
threats.mitigation: Require mTLS/JWT on write-capable endpoints, enforce schema/operation allowlists, validate write destinations, and run Iceberg connectors on isolated identities with least-privilege storage permissions.

threats.title: DDL operations allow schema manipulation (CREATE/DROP TABLE)
threats.description: v2.0 introduces CREATE TABLE and DROP TABLE DDL via FlightSQL and /v1/sql for Iceberg and Cayenne catalogs. An unauthenticated caller could create tables to exhaust storage, drop critical tables to cause data loss, or create tables pointing to attacker-controlled locations.
threats.mitigation: DDL is gated by catalog access mode (only catalogs with access: read_write_create accept DDL) and backend capability (currently Iceberg and Cayenne). Deploy behind authentication (API key, mTLS). Use storage-level IAM to restrict object creation. Monitor for unexpected DDL operations via task history and tracing. Consider an approval workflow or tighter access-mode policy for production environments.

threats.title: Distributed ingestion allows unauthorized data writes
threats.description: In v2.0, distributed ingestion allows executor nodes to write data to accelerated tables (including Cayenne). A compromised or rogue executor could inject malicious data, corrupt accelerated tables, or overwrite legitimate data during distributed ingestion.
threats.mitigation: Restrict executor registration to trusted nodes via allowlisting. Run cluster communication over private networks or with mTLS. Validate ingested data schemas before commit. Use Cayenne's WAL-based staged writes to detect and roll back partial/corrupt ingestions. Monitor for data anomalies post-ingestion.

threats.title: GCS credential exposure via data connector
threats.description: The GCS data connector (Alpha) requires Google Cloud credentials for bucket access. Service account keys or application default credentials could be leaked through error messages, verbose logging, or Spicepod configuration stored in version control.
threats.mitigation: Use Workload Identity Federation instead of long-lived service account keys. Store credentials in runtime-secrets, not in Spicepod YAML. Review error handling to ensure credential material is not logged. Apply least-privilege IAM roles scoped to specific buckets/prefixes.

threats.title: Search filter/column injection into planner
threats.description: Search request fields such as where_cond, keywords, and additional_columns flow into planning and can cause filter bypass, planning errors, or DoS if not validated.
threats.mitigation: Validate and quote identifiers; constrain filters and columns; sanitize planner errors.

threats.title: OIDC/JWT validation bypass accepts invalid tokens or exposes incorrect identity context
threats.description: Runtime bugs in issuer/audience validation, JWKS key handling, algorithm enforcement, expiry/not-before checks, or claim extraction can allow invalid tokens to authenticate or expose incorrect identity context.
threats.mitigation: Validate canonical issuer, configured audience, allowed algorithms, signature, exp/nbf, and JWKS keys; use bounded JWKS refresh and key selection by kid; test provider-specific tokens.

threats.title: Databricks auth header principal confusion
threats.description: User-controlled Databricks auth headers can confuse principal identity across Databricks-backed datasets if not scoped carefully.
threats.mitigation: Keep passthrough narrow and connector-specific; avoid generic credential forwarding; document scope.

threats.title: Protocol auth drift: API key/OIDC enforced on HTTP but not consistently mounted on Flight/FlightSQL/gRPC/internal services
threats.description: API key/OIDC auth may be enforced on one protocol but missing on another HTTP, Flight/FlightSQL, or gRPC surface.
threats.mitigation: Verify middleware mounting on all exposed protocols; keep cluster mTLS separate from external auth.

threats.title: OIDC bearer tokens or sensitive claims leak via logs, errors, telemetry, task history, or SQL-visible session_property()
threats.description: Bearer tokens or sensitive JWT claims may leak via logs, errors, telemetry, task history, or session_property outputs.
threats.mitigation: Redact Authorization headers; do not log tokens; avoid sensitive claims; restrict session_property exposure in views.

threats.title: JWKS retrieval/cache behavior can cause startup DoS, stale-key acceptance after revocation, or CPU amplification for malformed/no-kid tokens
threats.description: JWKS discovery/fetch can fail startup; stale cached keys may remain after revocation; no-kid tokens can amplify CPU by trying all keys.
threats.mitigation: Use bounded timeouts/retries, monitor refresh failures, prefer tokens with kid, and rate-limit invalid tokens.

threats.title: Public mTLS request mode admits anonymous callers while presented certs are promoted to a principal
threats.description: runtime.tls.client_auth_mode=request configures the public HTTP and Flight listeners to request a client certificate but still accept connections without one. Verified certs are promoted to an auth principal; anonymous callers continue to reach handlers. An operator may believe mTLS is enforced when only opportunistic client auth is in effect.
threats.mitigation: Use client_auth_mode=required for production mTLS enforcement; reserve request mode for migration/audit windows and pair it with logging that surfaces no-cert vs cert-bearing requests. Validation rejects request/required without a CA and rejects none with a CA.

data.name: Spice Cluster (Scheduler/Executors)
data.description: Ballista-based distributed query execution over gRPC with built-in mTLS on internal port 50052. v2.0 adds active-active HA via object-store-based scheduler registry, partition-aware data distribution with greedy set cover executor selection, ExpandSecret RPC for secret forwarding, bidirectional control streams, and distributed ingestion.

threats.title: Man-in-the-middle Data Sources
threats.description: A potential man-in-the-middle attack is possible where an attacker can inject themselves in the middle of the data source data stream to modify data in transit, causing Spice to return attacker-controlled payloads to the client applications.
threats.mitigation:
Connect to remote data sources using TLS/SSL
For data connectors that don't support TLS (FTP, Debezium) - connect over a secure network instead.

threats.title: Unauthenticated Iceberg write path abuse
threats.description: Because Iceberg supports writes, a compromised or unauthenticated caller could alter, overwrite, or delete Iceberg tables via the data connector.
threats.mitigation: Enforce authentication/authorization for Iceberg write endpoints, isolate Iceberg credentials, and apply storage-level ACLs and table-level governance.

threats.title: Model gateway key leakage and unbounded spend
threats.description: Hosted model and embedding providers are called with API keys. A compromised runtime, verbose logs, or replay of this channel can expose keys or allow attackers to trigger costly inference at scale.
threats.mitigation: Store provider keys in runtime-secrets, avoid logging headers/bodies, enforce egress allowlists and rate limits, and rotate provider credentials regularly.

data.name: Cluster Control Plane
data.description: gRPC communication between the Spice runtime and the Ballista scheduler, and between scheduler and executors. Network connections are executor-initiated (executor connects to scheduler); the gRPC stream itself is bidirectional. Scheduler→executor messages carry privileged commands (UpdatePartitions, CancelTasks, PollNow); executor→scheduler messages carry Heartbeat (every 10s) and metrics. Includes SchedulerGrpcServer (Ballista task dispatch) and ClusterService (GetAppDefinition, ExpandSecret, GetSchedulers, GetMetrics, ControlStream, AllocateInitialPartitions RPCs). Previously, GetAppDefinition and ExpandSecret were Flight Actions on the public port (50051); they are now served only on the internal mTLS-protected port (50052).

threats.title: Rogue cluster node injection
threats.description: Ballista scheduler and executor communication occurs over gRPC on a dedicated internal port (50052). Without mTLS enabled, a malicious host on the network could register a fake executor, intercept ExpandSecret RPCs to steal secrets, inject UpdatePartitions control-stream commands to reassign data, or read query data in transit. v2.0 increases risk: active-active HA with scheduler registry in object storage and dynamic cluster sizing mean executors join/leave frequently, and distributed ingestion allows executors to write data, not just read it.
threats.mitigation: Enable built-in mTLS (--node-mtls-ca-certificate-file, --node-mtls-certificate-file, --node-mtls-key-file), which is required by default for cluster mode (opt-out only via --allow-insecure-connections). Keep cluster traffic on a private network, restrict scheduler/executor discovery to allowlisted peers, and disable the cluster feature when not required.

threats.title: Control stream hijacking
threats.description: The bidirectional gRPC control stream carries privileged scheduler→executor commands (UpdatePartitions reassigns data ownership, CancelTasks aborts query execution, PollNow triggers immediate task polling) and executor→scheduler messages (Heartbeat every 10s for session liveness, periodic metrics reports). Without mTLS, an attacker could inject control-stream messages to reassign partitions to attacker-controlled nodes, cancel legitimate queries, or spoof heartbeats/metrics to keep stale sessions alive or poison scheduler state.
threats.mitigation: Enable built-in mTLS to authenticate both sides of the control stream. Deploy control-stream endpoints on the internal port (50052) not reachable from external networks. Monitor for unexpected control-stream commands via cluster observability. Implement command-level validation and rate limiting on the scheduler side.

data.name: Data Source(s)
data.description: Represents any number of data sources that Spice can connect to, including new GCS (Alpha) and DuckLake catalog connectors in v2.0.

data.name: Cayenne Accelerator (Vortex + SQLite)
data.description: Multi-file acceleration format combining Vortex columnar data and SQLite metadata. v2.0 RC adds staged WAL writes, DDL support, and distributed ingestion.

data.name: Hosted Model Provider
data.description: Third-party LLM/embedding APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, x.ai, etc.).

data.name: Acceleration Snapshots / Object Storage
data.description: Remote S3/GCS/object storage (or local file://) for snapshot bootstrap, Cayenne/Vortex artifacts, async query results (jobs/{job_id}/chunk_N.arrow with 12h default TTL), DuckLake data files, scheduler registry records (schedulers/{scheduler_id}.json), cluster metadata (metadata/cluster.json), job state (jobs/{job_id}.json), and partition metadata (accelerations/partitions/{table}.json). Uses ETag-based optimistic concurrency control (OCC) for state coordination.

data.name: Ballista Scheduler
data.description: Distributes query fragments and ingestion tasks to executors. v2.0 adds active-active HA via a scheduler registry (schedulers/{scheduler_id}.json, 30s default TTL) backed by either object storage or a local file:// directory. Manages partition assignments under accelerations/partitions/, serves secrets to executors via ExpandSecret RPC, and broadcasts UpdatePartitions/PollNow commands over bidirectional gRPC control streams. Listens on internal port 50052 (mTLS-protected by default).

threats.title: Secret forwarding interception via ExpandSecret RPC
threats.description: The scheduler serves secret values to executors via the ExpandSecret gRPC RPC on the internal port (50052). Secrets are transmitted in cleartext within the gRPC payload. Without mTLS, an attacker with network access could intercept ExpandSecret responses to capture data source credentials, API keys, and other secrets held in the scheduler's secret store.
threats.mitigation: Enable built-in mTLS for cluster communication (required by default; opt-out only via --allow-insecure-connections). Restrict network access to port 50052. Apply least-privilege secret scoping so executors only receive secrets required for their assigned partitions. Rotate secrets regularly. Monitor ExpandSecret call patterns for anomalies.

data.name: Ballista Executor
data.description: Executes query fragments and, in v2.0, performs distributed data ingestion into accelerated tables including Cayenne. Retrieves secrets from the scheduler via ExpandSecret RPC (secrets are never stored locally). Receives partition assignments and control commands (UpdatePartitions, CancelTasks) over a bidirectional gRPC control stream. Reports metrics back to the scheduler through the same control stream.

threats.title: Executor data exfiltration via distributed ingestion
threats.description: v2.0 executors now perform distributed ingestion, reading from data sources and writing to accelerated tables. A compromised executor could exfiltrate source data during ingestion, or redirect writes to an attacker-controlled destination.
threats.mitigation: Restrict executor network egress to only required data sources and object storage. Use IAM roles/instance profiles scoped to specific resources. Audit executor activity via cluster observability metrics. Run executors in isolated network segments.

threats.title: Shuffle data exposure in executor memory or storage
threats.description: During distributed query execution, intermediate shuffle data (partial query results exchanged between executors) is held in executor memory, local disk, or object storage in Arrow IPC or Vortex format. A compromised executor or an attacker with access to the executor's filesystem or object storage prefix could read sensitive intermediate results that would not otherwise be accessible.
threats.mitigation: Enable mTLS for all inter-executor data exchange (Flight shuffle). Use encrypted local storage for shuffle spill files. Apply short TTLs and automatic cleanup for shuffle artifacts in object storage. Restrict executor filesystem access and object storage prefixes with least-privilege IAM.

data.name: DuckLake Metadata (DuckDB)
data.description: DuckDB-backed metadata catalog for DuckLake lakehouse tables. Stores table schemas, file references, and snapshot history for time travel. New in v2.0.

data.name: Async Query Results
data.description: Async query results materialized to and retrieved from object storage.

diagrams.description: Models the components involved in federated query, acceleration, LLM inference, DDL operations, async query execution, and distributed execution for the Spice runtime v2.0.
